extractor.note: Read every paragraph carrying transcend- (outside transcendental), immanen-, surpass or overstep, in file order. Surpass in Lecture 29 (values surpassing values) and overstep in Lecture 34 are not the theme. No stratum: chronology.json has no entry for this commentary.

coverage_note: Term-led pass over the whole file (lines 1-674): every paragraph containing the transcendence family, including bare transcendent and immanent, was read; paragraphs without such a word were not read.

units.claim: Applied to the reduced field, immanent time is not a region of objective time but the form in which transcendental life presents itself to itself.
units.quote: immanent time is not a region of objective time but the form in which transcendental life presents itself to itself

units.claim: The transcendence of the world has no metaphysical mystery and is of the same genus as the transcendence of numbers and other irreal objects.
units.quote: The transcendence of the world has no metaphysical mystery: it is of another kind, but most generally of the same genus as the transcendence of numbers and other irreal objects.

units.claim: Before other egos are known, the real world reduces to a system of external experiences in which things are poles immanent to the system and transcendent to every single experience.
units.quote: The "immanent pole" formulation is precise: the thing is immanent to the system as its pole, transcendent to every single experience.

absences.expected_because: The possible non-existence of the world is argued here, and the later transition to egology treats the world's transcendence as that of a pole immanent to the system of experience.
